cli.browser.cleanup_blocked.note: detail is the daemon's refusal reason

cli.browser.live_tabs.note: count is the number of unowned live tabs

cli.browser.handles_redacted.note: provenance note under the live-tabs list

cli.browser.exact_cleanup.note: command hint; command tokens stay in situ

cli.browser.load_extension.note: follow-up step; command token in situ

cli.browser.installed_line.note: aligned label; value is a yes/no word

cli.browser.daemon_healthy.note: aligned label; value is a yes/no word

cli.browser.bridge_predates.note: aligned label; command token in situ

cli.browser.extension_connected.note: aligned label; value is a yes/no word

cli.browser.paired_line.note: aligned label; value is a yes/no word

cli.browser.driving_url.note: url is the page the bridge reports

cli.browser.heartbeat_stale.note: age is seconds; keep the ANSI codes exactly

cli.browser.heartbeat_fallback.note: consequence line under a stale heartbeat

cli.browser.heartbeat_repair.note: command hint; command token in situ

cli.browser.port_line.note: aligned label; port is a number

cli.browser.log_line.note: aligned label; log is a path

cli.browser.downloads_detail.note: size is bytes; audit is the audit filename

cli.browser.legacy_note.note: wrapped continuation; merged with 3708 so one sentence is one key

cli.browser.pair_no_extension.note: no extension paired; command token in situ

cli.browser.revoke_no_match.note: target echoes the user's typed token; keep ANSI codes

cli.browser.pairing_code.tone: plain, friendly, person-facing; often quoted verbatim by an agent
cli.browser.pairing_code.note: First line of the pairing block. {code} is six digits. Usually quoted verbatim by an agent to a person who never sees the terminal, so it must read as a complete sentence.

cli.browser.enter_code.tone: plain, friendly, person-facing; often quoted verbatim by an agent
cli.browser.enter_code.note: Tells the person where to type the code. The CLI just asked the extension to open its pairing tab. 'Pair' is the button label in the extension (English-only UI) — keep it as Pair.

cli.browser.pairing_code_labeled.tone: plain, friendly, person-facing; often quoted verbatim by an agent
cli.browser.pairing_code_labeled.note: One waiting browser: six-digit code, then its label (browser, extension version and short id, English, from the daemon). Keep the leading spaces and the gap.

cli.browser.enter_each_code.tone: plain, friendly, person-facing; often quoted verbatim by an agent
cli.browser.enter_each_code.note: Several browsers waiting. 'Pair' is the extension's English button label; keep it.

cli.browser.already_paired.tone: plain, friendly, person-facing; often quoted verbatim by an agent
cli.browser.already_paired.note: Already-paired answer, usually quoted to a person by an agent. "pair my browser" is the phrase the person says to the agent; keep it as a quoted phrase in the target language's natural wording for that request.

cli.browser.no_extension_waiting.tone: plain, friendly, person-facing; often quoted verbatim by an agent
cli.browser.no_extension_waiting.note: Nothing connected. The URL is the Chrome Web Store listing; keep it verbatim and keep a space after it. "pair my browser" is the phrase the person says to the agent.

cli.browser.now_driving.note: id is a short extension id

cli.browser.logs_missing.note: path is the daemon log path; command tokens in situ

cli.browser.cannot_run.note: command is a binary name; location is the log path; keep ANSI codes

cli.browser.note_prefix.note: note: prefix; warning is the uninstall warning; keep ANSI codes

cli.browser.usage.note: usage line; the brace group is literal (escaped)

cli.browser.drive_no_connected.note: target echoes the user's typed token

cli.browser.drive_no_single.note: target echoes the user's typed token

cli.browser.install_failed.note: fallback when the install result carries no error

cli.browser.status_yes.note: the word 'yes' on an aligned status row

cli.browser.status_no.note: the word 'no' on an aligned status row

cli.browser.no_tabs_known.note: empty-state line when the live-tabs list was read and is genuinely empty

cli.browser.no_tabs_unknown.note: empty-state line when the bridge did not answer; command token in situ. Wrapped with textwrap.fill(width=78) AFTER rendering, so line breaking stays a layout concern of the caller

cli.browser.could_not_pin_driver.note: fallback shown when the pin result carries no error text

cli.browser.cleanup_closed.note: cleanup outcome; wrapped with textwrap.fill by the caller, so widths stay layout

cli.browser.cleanup_retained.note: cleanup outcome; detail is the retention reason (free text, can quote an approval)

cli.browser.cleanup_tab_held_open.note: fallback retention reason when the bridge gave none

cli.browser.cleanup_pending.note: cleanup outcome; detail is the bridge's refusal; the generation sentence is advice the user acts on

cli.browser.cleanup_no_action.note: cleanup outcome; detail is why nothing was closed

cli.browser.enter_code_icon.tone: plain, friendly, person-facing; often quoted verbatim by an agent
cli.browser.enter_code_icon.note: Where to type the code when the installed extension is too old to open its own pairing tab. 'Pair' is the extension's English button label; keep it.

cli.browser.pair_no_page_hint.tone: plain, friendly, person-facing; often quoted verbatim by an agent
cli.browser.pair_no_page_hint.note: Fallback when the pairing tab did not appear. 'it' is the code.

cli.browser.pair_code_lifetime.tone: plain, friendly, person-facing; often quoted verbatim by an agent
cli.browser.pair_code_lifetime.note: Lifetime of the code plus the next step after pairing. {minutes} is 15 today. 'Allow' is the extension's English button label; keep it.

cli.browser.pair_several_header.tone: plain, friendly, person-facing; often quoted verbatim by an agent
cli.browser.pair_several_header.note: Header above one line per waiting browser.

cli.browser.pair_outdated.tone: plain, friendly, person-facing; often quoted verbatim by an agent
cli.browser.pair_outdated.note: Out-of-date extension. {label} is an English parenthesised label like '(Chrome extension 0.1.20 · jbadjeao…)'; {want} a version. chrome://extensions is typed in the address bar; keep it. 'Developer mode' and 'Update' are Chrome's control labels: use Chrome's localized label if known, else English.

cli.browser.pair_no_daemon.tone: plain, friendly, person-facing; often quoted verbatim by an agent
cli.browser.pair_no_daemon.note: The bridge service is not running. Commands stay verbatim.

cli.browser.pair_unreachable.tone: plain, friendly, person-facing; often quoted verbatim by an agent
cli.browser.pair_unreachable.note: {detail} is a short technical reason in English, kept in brackets at the end. Commands stay verbatim.

cli.browser.pair_after_reset.tone: plain, friendly, person-facing; often quoted verbatim by an agent
cli.browser.pair_after_reset.note: After --reset revoked every paired browser. Command stays verbatim.
